$description: Shelf design tokens (W3C DTCG format), direction Margin notes. Values come only from the approved DESIGN-BRIEF v1.0.0 and the CSS of its previews in docs/design/previews/v1/ (library.html, add-book.html); the radio-button tokens are the one addition, specified in UI-SPEC UX-106 because the browser-drawn radio fails WCAG 1.4.11 in the dark theme. Colour roles live under theme.light and theme.dark with identical paths and alias into color.palette; the product follows the device's prefers-color-scheme and has no theme switch. Dimensions use rem (1rem = 16px) or px as in the previews; the few em values (letter-spacing, underline offset) are relative to the element's own font size, as in the previews. Two sizes change at layout.breakpoint: '.narrow' applies below it, '.wide' at and above it. There are no motion, shadow or gradient tokens: the design uses none.

open_questions.question: Literata's optical-size axis (opsz 7-72). The previews were rendered with it (Google Fonts request opsz,wght with font-optical-sizing: auto), but the brief's approved default names only regular and italic with the variable weight axis. Without opsz, large headings and 16px notes render visibly differently from the previews.
open_questions.proposed_default: Self-host Literata regular and italic with both the weight axis (200-900) and the optical-size axis (7-72), so the product matches the approved previews.
open_questions.decide_in: Owner review of TOKENS v1.0.0; file size and format in architecture (Stage C)

open_questions.question: Hover and pressed (active) colours for buttons and links. The brief and the previews define none.
open_questions.proposed_default: No hover or pressed tokens: hover and press change nothing but the pointer cursor, as rendered.

open_questions.question: size.radio-dot (0.625rem) is not in the previews' CSS. The previews use the browser-drawn radio; 0.625rem is the solid dot measured in the rendered checked radio (previews/v1/add-book-desktop-light.png). The radio colours reuse existing roles (field border, field surface, accent).

palette.$description: Raw colours, named by the brief's roles (paper, ink, pencil, ink blue, error red, margin rose). Use them only through theme.light and theme.dark.

paper.$description: Day page: cool, slightly grey-green off-white.

page.$description: Page background (the sheet and the body).

primary.$description: Headings, titles, labels, typed text, the wordmark, the Reading note.

muted.$description: Authors, Want to read and Finished notes, the line under the heading.

error.$description: Field errors and the save-failure message.

margin-rule.$description: The margin line. Decorative only; never carries meaning.

body.$description: The only family. Literata (SIL OFL) is self-hosted, regular and italic with the variable weight axis; no font service (NFR-004). Optical-size axis: TQ-1.

regular.$description: Body text, typed text, radio labels, authors, notes other than Reading.

medium.$description: Book titles, the wordmark, text links.

semibold.$description: Field labels, the status legend, filled buttons, error messages.

reading.$description: The Reading note, which stands out by weight.

field.$description: Field labels, the status legend, typed text, radio labels.

breakpoint.$description: 768px. Below it the phone layout (.narrow); at and above it the desktop layout (.wide).

measure.$description: Width of the text column at most.

narrow.$description: On phones the margin is a thin strip; nothing sits in it.

margin-inset.$description: Space between right-aligned margin content and the rule (desktop).

field-error-offset.$description: Top offset of a field error in the margin, so its first line sits level with the field's text (desktop).

target-min.$description: 44px: minimum height of every button, link and radio row.

focus.$description: Focus outline corners on elements without a radius of their own (links, the wordmark link).
